flows.representativeInput: [AC:spec-9-1] tests/runtime-archive-named-files.test.ts:265 and probe sections A and H
flows.expected: After a real --apply, /* x */ then code, a .ts #field line and a bare * line in a template literal make next name that test and line; a .py # test, a .ts // Spec test and a .ts * line inside an open /** */ block are comment-only.

observations.actual: 21 of 21 tests in 2 files pass, including [AC:spec-9-1]: p1/p2/p3 each give "1 test still names" with the exact file:line; test_q1.py, q2.test.ts, q3.test.ts singly and together give the comment-only message.

Spec 1 reviewer probe section A re-run with the new wording: the three former false comment-only cases (/* */ then code, #dir private field, * bullet in a template literal) are now called code at the right line; the other A cases stay ok; the block body line without a leading * stays code (safe direction). Hunt section H: */ then code on a later line, code after */ on the closing line, * after the block closed, <!-- --> then code (same and later line), # lines in .ts/.js/.mjs, CRLF files (// then code, /** block then code, */ code on the closing line, .py # then string), /*/ opener, in-block "* a */ code" are all called code. Remaining comment-only calls on code that reads the folder: a // line and a /*-opened fake block inside a template literal, a # line inside a Python triple-quoted string, a CR-only file, and a // line with U+2028 (see findings).

flows.expected: All-comment-only next says no path change looks needed and to run the gate, without "Leave their paths as they are".

observations.actual: [AC:spec-9-2] passes. archive.mjs:612 now reads "...only in comments, so no path change looks needed. Still run the gate: a red test means one reads the folder..."; the old sentence is gone. The [AC:spec-1-5] assertion changed from "need no change" to "no path change looks needed", a class-1 change the Test changes section allows.

Every comment-only call in the probe prints the run-the-gate text; the mixed case (one comment-only, one code test) still names only the code test and keeps its "The other listed tests ... need no change" tail.

flows.expected: Preview from src/deep equals the root preview; --apply from src/deep moves the folder at the root and creates nothing under src/deep.

observations.actual: [AC:spec-9-3] passes: both previews exit 0 with empty stderr and equal JSON; apply from src/deep returns archived, docs/features/x is gone, docs/archive/x exists, and find in src/deep lists only keep.txt.

limits: Gate not run (reviewer runs only the spec's own tests, per the brief); due at the coordinator's gate.

findings.summary: Dangerous direction, reproducible (probe H9, H10): a line that starts with // inside a template literal, or a * line after a /* line inside a template literal, is called a comment although it is string content a test can read. This follows the spec's rules (a) and (c) as written, and the new message now says to run the gate, which catches a real read. Lexing strings is out of this spec's scope.
findings.assumption: Rules (a) and (c) are the owner-approved definition; the run-the-gate sentence is the intended safety net.

findings.summary: Dangerous direction, reproducible (probe H20): a # line inside a Python triple-quoted string is called a comment; rule (d) allows it by extension alone. Same safety net as f1.

Dangerous direction, rare (probe H15, H24): lines split on 
 only (pre-existing, unchanged), so a CR-only file, or a // line followed by U+2028 and code, reads as one comment line. CRLF works (probe H11-H14). Splitting on /
||
| | / would close it; namedFiles (archive.mjs:554) splits the same way.

Safe direction only: a block body line without a leading *, a block reopened after a closed one on the same line, and a block opened after code on a line are called code (probe A p2, H16, H19). Matches the spec's "any doubt counts as code".

Checked: the spec 9 commit 592ba98 changes only lines 565-612 (isCommentLine replaced by commentLines, nextSteps); namedFiles (541-561) and folderPatterns are untouched, and the [AC:spec-1-5] namedFiles-matches-preview assertion is unchanged.
